title: Prion diseases and adult neurometabolic storage disorders

steps.tx: Sporadic **Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease** manifests with rapidly progressive dementia, **startle myoclonus**, ataxia, and visual abnormalities, leading to death typically within 6 to 12 months from symptom onset due to scrapie prion propagation. The relentless clinical course demands prompt diagnostic evaluation to exclude treatable autoimmune mimics.

steps.tx: Brain MRI in Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease demonstrates striking **cortical ribboning** on DWI along cerebral gyri, hyperintensity in the caudate and putamen, and the characteristic **hockey-stick sign** in the pulvinar and dorsomedial thalamic nuclei in variant CJD. Diffusion-weighted imaging remains the most sensitive imaging sequence for detecting early cortical and striatal abnormalities.

steps.tx: Real-time quaking-induced conversion, designated as **RT-QuIC** in CSF, provides definitive diagnosis of sporadic CJD with greater than 95% sensitivity and near 100% specificity by detecting pathologically misfolded scrapie **prion protein**. This revolutionary non-invasive assay has largely supplanted brain biopsy in suspected cases.

steps.tx: Peroxisomal metabolic dysfunction causes childhood and adult demyelination. **Adrenoleukodystrophy** is caused by ABCD1 gene mutations impairing peroxisomal beta-oxidation, leading to accumulation of very long chain **fatty acids** with posterior white matter demyelination and adrenal insufficiency. Plasma very long chain fatty acid profiling provides rapid biochemical diagnostic confirmation.

steps.tx: **Gaucher disease** type 1 is the most common lysosomal storage disease, caused by **glucocerebrosidase** deficiency, presenting with hepatosplenomegaly, bone crises, Erlenmeyer flask deformity, and lipid-laden Gaucher cells with crinkled paper appearance. Enzyme replacement therapy with imiglucerase substantially reverses organomegaly, cytopenias, and skeletal complications.

steps.tx: **Niemann-Pick** disease type C is a lysosomal lipid trafficking disorder caused by mutations in NPC1 or NPC2, presenting with progressive supranuclear **vertical gaze** palsy, cerebellar ataxia, cognitive decline, and gelastic cataplexy. Miglustat serves as disease-specific substrate reduction therapy that stabilizes neurological manifestations.

steps.tx: **Tay-Sachs** disease results from hexosaminidase A deficiency with accumulation of GM2 ganglioside, featuring rapid neurodegeneration, hyperacusis, and a pathognomonic **cherry-red spot** at the macula without accompanying hepatosplenomegaly in affected infants. Progressive macrocephaly typically develops by two years of age due to exuberant reactive cerebral gliosis.

steps.tx: **Krabbe disease**, also called globoid cell leukodystrophy, results from **galactocerebrosidase** deficiency, producing severe white matter demyelination with accumulation of cytotoxic psychosine and globoid multinucleated macrophages on central nervous system histology. Hematopoietic stem cell transplantation before symptom onset offers the only proven strategy to arrest demyelination.
